hook.convey: two same-size wholes, one cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 8 → 8 is the bigger number, yet each of its parts is smaller → which single part to pick is the question

use.hi: Socho, do bilkul ek jaise cake. Ek ke 4 barabar tukde kiye, doosre ke 8. Tumhe bas ek tukda milega, kisi bhi cake se.
use.en: Picture two cakes, exactly alike. One is cut into 4 equal pieces, the other into 8. You get just one piece, from either cake.

use.hi: Tumhare paas do drawing sheet hain, bilkul ek jaisi. Ek ko 4 barabar hisson mein baanto, doosri ko 8 mein. Colour sirf ek hissa karna hai, kisi ek sheet ka.
use.en: You have two drawing sheets, exactly alike. Split one into 4 equal parts, the other into 8. You colour just one part, of one sheet.

explain.convey: one bar = one whole; 4 equal parts; 1 shaded part = 1/4; bottom number = how many equal parts the whole is cut into → predict: more cuts of the same bar, one part smaller

point.hi: Upar yeh rahi ek poori patti. 4 barabar hisse, aur ek mein rang bhara hai. Woh ek hissa 1/4 hai. Bhinn ke neeche ka 4 matlab patti ke 4 barabar tukde.
point.en: Up top is one whole bar. 4 equal parts, and one is coloured in. That one part is 1/4. The 4 at the bottom of the fraction means the bar's 4 equal pieces.

prompt.hi: Neeche wahi patti 8 barabar hisson mein kati hai. Ab iska ek hissa upar wale ek hisse se bada hai ya chhota?
prompt.en: Below, the same bar is cut into 8 equal parts. Is one part of it bigger or smaller than one part on top?

why.hi: dono patti barabar lambi hain, par upar wali 4 hisson mein hai, neeche wali 8 mein, isliye neeche ka hissa chhota hai
why.en: both bars are equally long, but the top one has 4 parts, the lower 8, so a lower part is smaller

simpler.hi: Ek hi roti socho, pehle 4 log baantein, phir 8 log. Log badhe, toh har ek ke haath ka tukda kaisa hua, yeh socho.
simpler.en: Think of one roti, shared first by 4 people, then by 8. More people, so what happens to each person's piece, think about that.

explain.convey: same-size bar now in 8 equal parts → 1 part = 1/8 → the bars lie one under the other, so two lower parts line up under one top part → which top fraction do two 1/8 parts make

point.hi: Ab wahi patti, par 8 barabar hisse, toh ek hissa 1/8. Dono patti ek jitni lambi hain, isliye neeche ke hisse upar wale hisson ke theek neeche baithte hain.
point.en: Now the same bar, but in 8 equal parts, so one part is 1/8. Both bars are the same length, so the parts below sit right under the parts on top.

prompt.hi: Neeche ke pehle do 1/8 hisse jodo. Woh milkar upar wali patti ka kaunsa bhinn banate hain?
prompt.en: Join the first two 1/8 parts below. Together, which fraction of the top bar do they make?

why.hi: neeche ke do 1/8 hisse milkar upar ke ek hisse jitne lambe hain, aur upar ka woh hissa 1/4 hai
why.en: two 1/8 parts below together are as long as one part on top, and that top part is 1/4

simpler.hi: Neeche ke pehle do hisson par ungli rakho, aur dekho upar ki patti ka kitna hissa theek unke upar hai.
simpler.en: Put a finger on the first two parts below, and see how much of the top bar sits right above them.

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line, thirds above and sevenths below → further from 0 = bigger; by that rule 1/8 < 1/4 → which of 1/3, 1/7 stops further from 0

point.hi: Ab ek sankhya rekha lo, 0 se 1 tak. Upar ise 3 barabar hisson mein kaata hai, neeche 7 mein. Rekha ka niyam simple hai: zero se jitna door, utna bada. Isi niyam se, 1/8 aur 1/4 ko kisi bhi rekha par rakho, toh 1/8 zero ke zyada paas rukega: 1/8 < 1/4.
point.en: Now take a number line, 0 to 1. Along the top it's cut into 3 equal parts, along the bottom into 7. The line's rule is simple: the further from zero, the bigger. By that rule, put 1/8 and 1/4 on any line and 1/8 stops closer to zero: 1/8 < 1/4.

prompt.hi: Isi rekha par, zero se zyada door kaun rukega, 1/3 ya 1/7?
prompt.en: On this line, which one stops further from zero, 1/3 or 1/7?

why.hi: 1/3 ka hissa 1/7 ke hisse se bada hai, toh 1/3 zero se aage jaakar rukta hai
why.en: a 1/3 part is bigger than a 1/7 part, so 1/3 stops further from zero

simpler.hi: Rekha dekho: upar 3 hisse, neeche 7. Jiske hisse kam, uska pehla kadam lamba.
simpler.en: Look at the line: 3 parts on top, 7 below. Fewer parts means a longer first step.

problem.hi: Rahul aur Sana ke paas ek jaise chocolate bar hain. Rahul ko apne bar ka 1/8 mila, Sana ko apne ka 1/2. Bada tukda kiske paas hai?
problem.en: Rahul and Sana have identical chocolate bars. Rahul gets 1/8 of his bar, Sana gets 1/2 of hers. Who has the bigger piece?

simpler.hi: Rahul aur Sana ke bar ek jitne hain. Rahul ko 1/8 mila, Sana ko 1/2, aur dekhna hai kiska tukda bada hai.
simpler.en: Rahul's and Sana's bars are the same size. Rahul got 1/8, Sana 1/2, and we see whose piece is bigger.

givens.hi: bar barabar hain, toh mukabla sirf 1/8 aur 1/2 ka hai
givens.en: the bars match, so it's just 1/8 against 1/2

do.hi: Pehle dono ka upar wala number dekho
do.en: First look at the top number of both

steps.result: dono mein 1, yaani dono ko ek-ek tukda

why.hi: upar ka number batata hai kitne tukde mile, aur ek-ek mile, toh ab baat sirf size ki hai
why.en: the top number says how many pieces each got, and it's one each, so now it's only about size

simpler.hi: Upar 1 aur 1, matlab dono ke haath ek-ek tukda. Ab socho, kiska tukda mota.
simpler.en: 1 on top and 1 on top, so each got one piece. Now think whose piece is chunkier.

do.hi: Phir dekho, kiska bar kitne hisson mein kata: upar wala Rahul ka, neeche wala Sana ka
do.en: Then see how many parts each bar was cut into: the top one is Rahul's, the bottom one Sana's

steps.result: Rahul ka bar 8 hisson mein, Sana ka sirf 2 mein

why.hi: hisson ki ginti se hi pata chalta hai ki ek tukda kitna bada hai
why.en: the number of parts is what tells you how big one piece is

simpler.hi: 8 mein kata bar, matlab patle-patle tukde. 2 mein kata, matlab mote tukde.
simpler.en: A bar cut into 8 gives thin pieces. Cut into 2, it gives chunky ones.

prompt.hi: Tum batao, bada tukda kisko mila, Rahul ko ya Sana ko?
prompt.en: Now you tell me, who got the bigger piece, Rahul or Sana?

why.hi: Sana ka bar sirf 2 hisson mein kata hai, isliye uska ek tukda Rahul ke 8 hisson wale tukde se bada hai
why.en: Sana's bar is cut into only 2 parts, so her piece is bigger than Rahul's piece from 8 parts

simpler.hi: Bar dono barabar hain. Jo bar kam hisson mein kata, uska tukda mota.
simpler.en: The bars are equal. The bar cut into fewer parts gives the chunkier piece.

why.hi: 8 bada number hai, par 8 hisson wale bar ka tukda chhota hota hai, isliye 1/8 chhota aur 1/2 bada
why.en: 8 is the bigger number, but a bar cut into 8 has smaller pieces, so 1/8 is smaller and 1/2 bigger

prompt.hi: Do roti, bilkul ek jaisi. Ek ke 10 barabar tukde hain, doosri ke 5. Kaunsa ek tukda bada hai, 1/10 ya 1/5?
prompt.en: Two rotis, exactly alike. One is in 10 equal pieces, the other in 5. Which single piece is bigger, 1/10 or 1/5?

accept: the piece from the roti cut into 5

why.hi: 5 tukdon wali roti ka 1/5, 10 tukdon wali roti ke 1/10 se do guna bada hai
why.en: a 1/5 piece of the 5-piece roti is twice a 1/10 piece of the 10-piece roti

simpler.hi: Dono roti ek jaisi hain. Jitne kam log baantenge, har ek ko utna bada tukda milega.
simpler.en: Both rotis are alike. The fewer people sharing one, the bigger each piece.

prompt.hi: Ek hi poore ke yeh teen bhinn lo: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6. Sabse chhote se shuru karke kram se lagao.
prompt.en: Take these three fractions of the same whole: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6. Put them in order, starting from the smallest.

why.hi: poora ek ho toh 1/12 ke tukde sabse chhote, 1/6 beech mein, aur 1/3 sabse bade
why.en: in one whole, 1/12 pieces are the smallest, 1/6 sits in the middle, and 1/3 is the biggest

simpler.hi: Sirf neeche ke number dekho: teen, barah, chhe. Jiska neeche sabse bada, uska tukda sabse chhota.
simpler.en: Look only at the bottom numbers: three, twelve, six. The biggest bottom number has the smallest piece.

prompt.hi: Yeh rekha 0 se 1 tak 3 barabar hisson mein bati hai, aur 0 ke baad pehle nishaan par koi number nahi likha. Woh pehla nishaan 1/5 se bada hai ya chhota?
prompt.en: This line from 0 to 1 is cut into 3 equal parts, and the first mark after 0 has a question mark on it. Is that question-mark point bigger or smaller than 1/5?

why.hi: woh nishaan 1/3 hai, aur 3 hisson wala tukda 5 hisson wale tukde se bada hota hai, isliye woh 1/5 se bada
why.en: that mark is 1/3, and a piece from 3 parts beats a piece from 5 parts, so it is bigger

simpler.hi: Pehle us nishaan ka naam socho: poore ke 3 hisson mein se pehla hissa. Phir use 1/5 ke saath rakh kar dekho.
simpler.en: First name that mark: it's the first of the whole's 3 parts. Then hold it up against 1/5.

say.hi: Rekha dekho, 0 se 1 tak. Neeche ise 12 barabar hisson mein kaata hai. 12 ek bada number hai, par uska ek hissa zero ke bilkul paas ruk jaata hai. Hisse jitne zyada, har tukda utna chhota.

simpler.en: Think of one roti: shared by 12, everyone gets a tiny bit; shared by two, it's half each.

prompt.hi: Patang ki do dor, ek jitni lambi. Ek dor se 1/8 kaata, doosri se 1/12. Kaunsa tukda lamba, 1/8 wala ya 1/12 wala?
prompt.en: Two equally long kite strings. 1/8 is cut from one, 1/12 from the other. Which piece is longer, the 1/8 or the 1/12?

why.hi: ek jitni dor mein 8 hisse 12 hisson se kam hain, toh 1/8 ka hissa 1/12 wale se lamba
why.en: from strings of one length, 8 parts are fewer than 12, so a 1/8 piece is longer than a 1/12 piece

simpler.hi: Rekha par upar ke hisse neeche walon se bade hain. Jiske hisse kam, uska ek hissa bada.
simpler.en: On the line, the parts on top are bigger than those below. Fewer parts means a bigger single part.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak har baar sirf ek tukda tha, toh tukde ka size hi sab tay karta tha. Agla khel alag hai: neeche ka number same, upar ka alag.
bridgeToNext.en: Until now it was always one piece, so the piece size settled everything. Next is a different game: the same bottom number, different top numbers.

simpler.hi: Ab tak har baar ek hi tukda tha. Ab neeche ka number same hoga, upar ka alag.
simpler.en: So far it was always one piece. Now the bottom number is the same and the top one differs.

hook.convey: two same-size wholes, each cut into 7 equal parts; one person takes 2 parts of one, another takes 4 parts of the other → same-size parts, so who has more is settled by the top number alone

use.hi: {friend} aur Sohan ke saamne do ek jaise cake hain, dono 7 barabar tukdon mein kate. {friend} ne 2 tukde khaaye, Sohan ne 4.
use.en: {friend} and Sohan each have a cake, both alike, both cut into 7 equal pieces. {friend} ate 2 pieces, Sohan ate 4.

use.hi: Ritu aur Vikram ke garden ek jitne bade hain, dono mein 7 barabar kyariyan. Ritu ne 2 kyariyon mein flower lagaye, Vikram ne 4 mein.
use.en: Ritu's and Vikram's gardens are the same size, each with 7 equal beds. Ritu planted flowers in 2 beds, Vikram in 4.

explain.convey: bar in 7 equal parts → each part 1/7; 2 shaded = 2/7 = two 1/7 parts; top number = how many of those equal parts are taken

point.hi: Pehli patti ke 7 barabar hisse hain, har ek 1/7. 2 mein rang hai, toh yeh 2/7. Bhinn ke upar ka 2 bas ginta hai ki kitne hisse liye.
point.en: The first bar has 7 equal parts, each one 1/7. 2 are coloured, so this is 2/7. The 2 on top of the fraction just counts how many parts we took.

prompt.hi: Doosri patti bhi bilkul waisi hai. Agar iske 4 hisson mein rang bhar dein, toh kaunsa bhinn banega?
prompt.en: The second bar is just the same. If we colour 4 of its parts, which fraction do we get?

why.hi: hisse wahi 7 hain, rang ab 4 mein, toh 4/7
why.en: there are still 7 parts, now 4 are coloured, so 4/7

simpler.hi: Bhinn ke neeche wahi 7 rahega, patti waisi hi hai. Upar bas utne gino jitne hisson mein rang bharoge.
simpler.en: The bottom stays 7, the bar is just the same. On top, just count how many parts you'd colour.

explain.convey: the same sevenths as steps on a 0-to-1 line: every step 1/7, 4/7 = 4 steps → part size unchanged, only the count changes → the 'both are sevenths, so equal' belief tested

point.hi: Ab yahi hisse ek sankhya rekha par: 0 se 1 tak 7 barabar kadam, har kadam 1/7. 4/7 tak pahunchne mein 4 kadam lagte hain. Kadam sab ek hi size ke, bas ginti badalti hai.
point.en: Now these parts on a number line: 0 to 1 in 7 equal steps, each step 1/7. Reaching 4/7 takes 4 steps. The steps are all one size; only the count changes.

prompt.hi: Rohan kehta hai, 2/7 aur 4/7 barabar hain, dono sevenths hi toh hain. Kya Rohan sahi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Rohan says 2/7 and 4/7 are equal, since both are sevenths. Is Rohan right, yes or no?

why.hi: sevenths dono hain, par ginti alag hai: 4/7 mein 4 hisse, 2/7 mein bas 2
why.en: both are sevenths, but the counts differ: 4/7 has 4 parts, 2/7 only 2

simpler.hi: Rekha ke kadam sab ek size ke hain. Ab bas kadam gino.
simpler.en: The steps on the line are all one size. Now just count the steps.

explain.convey: a 0-to-1 line in fifths: further from 0 = bigger; same bottom number → the top number says how many steps → 2/5 vs 4/5

point.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha 0 se 1 tak 5 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Rekha par zero se jitna door, utna bada. Neeche ka number same ho, toh faisla upar wala number karta hai: woh batata hai kitne kadam chalna hai.
point.en: This number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 5 equal parts. On a line, the further from zero, the bigger. When the bottom number is the same, the top number decides: it says how many steps to take.

prompt.hi: Isi rekha par zero se zyada door kaun hoga, 2/5 ya 4/5?
prompt.en: On this line, which is further from zero, 2/5 or 4/5?

why.hi: kadam dono ke 1/5 ke hain, aur 4/5 chaar kadam chalta hai, 2/5 sirf do
why.en: both step in 1/5s, and 4/5 takes four steps, 2/5 only two

simpler.hi: Har kadam ek jaisa hai. Jo zyada kadam chale, woh zero se zyada door pahunche.
simpler.en: Every step is the same size. Whoever takes more steps ends up further from zero.

explain.convey: two equal strips, one in 3 parts, one in 10 → different bottom numbers, different-size pieces → counting alone decides nothing; same-size pieces only with the same bottom number → 2/3 vs 3/10

point.hi: Yeh do barabar patti dekho: upar wali 3 hisson mein kati hai, neeche wali 10 mein. Bhinn ke neeche ke number alag hain, toh alag size ke hisse: 10 wali ke hisse patle, 3 wali ke mote. Same size ke hisse tabhi hote hain jab bhinn ke neeche ka number same ho. Yahan sirf ginne se faisla nahi hota.
point.en: Look at these two equal bars: the top one cut into 3 parts, the bottom one into 10. The fractions' bottom numbers differ, so these are different-size pieces: the 10-bar's are thin, the 3-bar's chunky. You only get same-size pieces when the bottom number matches. Here, counting alone doesn't decide.

prompt.hi: Ek bar ka 2/3 lo, aur usi size ke doosre bar ka 3/10. Hisse 3/10 mein zyada hain. Par bada kaun hai, 2/3 ya 3/10?
prompt.en: Take 2/3 of one bar, and 3/10 of another bar the same size. 3/10 has more pieces. But which is bigger, 2/3 or 3/10?

why.hi: 2/3 aadhe se aage nikal jaata hai, aur 3/10 aadhe, yaani 5/10, tak bhi nahi pahunchta
why.en: 2/3 goes past a half, while 3/10 doesn't even reach a half, which is 5/10

simpler.hi: Aadha ek achhi pehchaan hai. Har patti ka aadha socho, aur dekho kaun aadhe se aage hai, kaun peeche.
simpler.en: Half is a handy guide. Picture each bar's half, and see which one gets past it and which falls short.

problem.en: Meena and Raju have identical cakes. Meena ate 5/8 of hers, Raju 3/8 of his. Who ate less cake?

simpler.hi: Dono ke cake same size ke hain. Meena ne 5/8 khaya, Raju ne 3/8, aur dekhna hai kisne kam khaya.
simpler.en: Meena's and Raju's cakes are the same. Meena ate 5/8, Raju 3/8, and we see who ate less.

givens.hi: hamare paas bas do bhinn hain, 5/8 aur 3/8, aur dono ka poora ek jaisa
givens.en: all we have are two fractions, 5/8 and 3/8, of the same-size whole

why.hi: dono poore ek jaise hain aur dono 8 barabar tukdon mein bate hain

simpler.hi: Neeche dono jagah 8 hai. Matlab har tukda 1/8, chahe Meena ka ho ya Raju ka.
simpler.en: Both have 8 at the bottom. So every piece is 1/8, whether it's Meena's or Raju's.

steps.result: Meena ke 1/8 wale 5 tukde, Raju ke 3

why.hi: upar ka number gin kar batata hai kitne tukde khaye gaye
why.en: the top number counts the pieces eaten

simpler.hi: Upar ka number bas ginti hai. 5 tukde ek taraf, 3 tukde doosri taraf.
simpler.en: The top number is just a count. 5 pieces on one side, 3 on the other.

prompt.hi: Toh kam cake kiske hisse aaya, Meena ke ya Raju ke?
prompt.en: So who ended up with less cake, Meena or Raju?

why.hi: dono ke tukde ek hi size ke hain, aur Raju ke sirf 3 tukde hain jabki Meena ke 5
why.en: both have pieces of the same size, and Raju has only 3 of them while Meena has 5

simpler.hi: Tukde ek jaise hain, toh kam tukde matlab kam hissa. Ab 5 aur 3 milao.
simpler.en: The pieces match, so fewer pieces means a smaller share. Now set 5 against 3.

why.hi: tukde ek size ke hain aur Raju ke kam hain, isliye rekha par bhi 3/8 pehle aata hai, 5/8 baad mein
why.en: the pieces are one size and Raju has fewer, so on the line too 3/8 comes before 5/8

prompt.en: Meena and her brother have identical cakes. Meena ate 2/6 of hers, her brother 4/6 of his. Who ate more: Meena, her brother, or both the same?

why.hi: dono ke tukde 1/6 ke hain, aur bhai ke 4/6, Meena ke 2/6 se zyada
why.en: both ate 1/6 pieces, and the brother's 4/6 beats Meena's 2/6

simpler.hi: Cake ek jaise, tukde bhi ek size ke. Bas upar wale number milao.

simpler.hi: 10 wale cake ka ek tukda, 5 wale cake ke tukde ka aadha hai. Tukde alag size ke hain, isliye sirf ginti se faisla nahi hota.

why.hi: 5/6 se bas 1/6 kam hai, 3/4 se poora 1/4, aur 1/6 ka gap chhota hai
why.en: 5/6 is short by just 1/6, 3/4 by a whole 1/4, and the 1/6 gap is smaller

simpler.en: Look at what's missing. The line has 4 parts on top, 6 below: one part below is smaller than one on top.

say.hi: Bhinn ke neeche ka 7 batata hai ki poore ke 7 barabar hisse hain, toh rekha ka har kadam 1/7 ka hai. Bhinn ke upar ka number ginta hai kitne kadam chale. Kadam ek jaise hon, toh zyada kadam matlab zero se zyada door.

prompt.hi: Ribbon ke 7 barabar tukde hain. {friend} ne 2 liye, Gopi ne 6. Zyada ribbon kiske paas, {friend} ke ya Gopi ke?

why.hi: har tukda ribbon ka 1/7 hai, aur Gopi ka 6/7, 2/7 se zyada hai

simpler.hi: Ribbon ke sab tukde ek size ke hain, jaise rekha ke kadam. Toh jiske haath zyada tukde, uske paas zyada ribbon.
simpler.en: All the ribbon pieces are one size, like the steps on the line. So whoever holds more pieces has more ribbon.

remediation.move: two equal strips, 4 parts and 12: one 1/4 part = three 1/12 parts → 2/12, two pieces, is still less than one 1/4 → the count of pieces decides only when the pieces are the same size, i.e. same bottom number

say.hi: Upar ki patti 4 hisson mein kati hai, neeche ki 12 mein. Upar ka ek hissa neeche ke teen tukdon jitna lamba hai. Toh neeche ke do tukde bhi upar ke ek tukde se chhote hain. Tukde tabhi gino, jab sab ek size ke hon.
say.en: The top bar is cut into 4 parts, the bottom one into 12. One part on top is as long as three parts below. So even two pieces below are smaller than one piece on top. Count pieces only when they're all one size.

simpler.hi: Neeche ke tukde chhote hain, upar ke bade. Do chhote tukde milkar bhi ek bade tak nahi pahunchte.
simpler.en: The pieces below are small, the ones on top big. Two small ones together don't even reach one big one.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaisi patti: ek ke 4 barabar hisse, doosri ke 12. Kaun zyada hai, 2/4 ya 5/12?
prompt.en: Two identical strips, one cut into 4 equal parts, one into 12. Which is more, 2/4 or 5/12?

say.hi: Upar ki patti 8 hisson mein hai, neeche ki 10 mein. Socho, dono mein se ek-ek hissa hata do. Ginti mat dekho, gayab hisse ka size dekho: jiski kami chhoti, woh 1 ke zyada paas.
say.en: The top bar is in 8 parts, the bottom in 10. Imagine taking one part from each. Don't look at the count, look at the size of the missing part: the smaller gap is closer to 1.

simpler.hi: Dono se ek-ek hissa hi gaya. Ab bas dekho, kiska gaya hissa mota tha.
simpler.en: Each lost just one part. Now only see whose missing part was thicker.

prompt.hi: Do patti, ek jitni lambi. Ek ke 8 barabar hisse, doosri ke 10. Dono mein bas ek hissa kam. Kaunsa bada, 7/8 ya 9/10?

why.hi: 9/10 se bas 1/10 kam hai, 7/8 se 1/8, aur 1/10 wala gap chhota hai

simpler.hi: Dono patti se ek-ek hissa gayab hai. 8 wali patti ka hissa 10 wali se mota, toh jiska mota hissa gayab, woh chhota.
simpler.en: Both are missing one part. A part of the 8-strip is chunkier than one of the 10-strip, so the one missing the chunkier part is smaller.

bridgeToNext.hi: Neeche ka number same tha, toh upar wale ne faisla kiya. Ab ulta khel: upar ka number same, neeche ka alag.
bridgeToNext.en: When the bottom number matched, the top one decided. Now the flip side: the top number matches, the bottom one differs.

simpler.hi: Pehle neeche ka number same tha. Ab upar ka number same hoga, neeche ka alag.
simpler.en: Before, the bottom number matched. Now the top number matches and the bottom one differs.

point.en: The top bar is in 5 equal parts, so each part is 1/5. Three parts are coloured: 3/5.

prompt.hi: Neeche isi size ki patti 8 barabar hisson mein kati hai, aur 3 mein rang hai. Yeh kaunsa bhinn hai?

simpler.hi: Bhinn mein neeche wahi aata hai jitne hisse kate, upar utne jitne rang wale. Neeche wali patti mein 8 kate, 3 rang wale.
simpler.en: In a fraction, the bottom is how many parts were cut, the top how many are coloured. In the lower bar, 8 cut and 3 coloured.

explain.convey: fifths above, eighths below on one 0-to-1 line: 3/8 = three steps below; same count 3, different step size → the 'both are 3 pieces, so equal' belief tested

point.hi: Ab dono ko ek sankhya rekha par dekho, 0 se 1 tak: upar 5 barabar hisse, har ek 1/5; neeche 8, har ek 1/8. 3/8 matlab neeche ke teen kadam. Ginti dono mein 3 hi hai, par kadam ka size alag hai.
point.en: Now see both on a number line, 0 to 1: 5 equal parts on top, each 1/5; 8 below, each 1/8. 3/8 means three steps along the bottom. The count is 3 in both, but the step size differs.

point.en: When the count of pieces matches, piece size decides. The strip cut into fewer parts has bigger pieces, so the same number of pieces is more there.

simpler.hi: Ginti dono mein 2 hai. Ab bas yeh socho: 5 hisson wali patti ka ek hissa bada hai, ya 9 wali ka.
simpler.en: The count is 2 in both. Now just think which is bigger: one part of the 5-part bar, or one of the 9-part bar.

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line, quarters above and eighths below: the first top mark 1/4 sits over 2/8 → every quarter is two eighths → transfer: 2/4 vs 5/8 on the same line
